lectures.title: Insert a Node in Binary Heap

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at inserting a node to binary heap.
So let's say we have a binary heap like this.
So we can easily see that this is max heap because the greatest element in the heap is located at the
root of this binary heap.
So this means that this is max heap.
So whenever we are inserting a new node to this binary heap, we are going to insert it to the next
vacant place.
So let's say we want to insert 100 over here.
Now the next vacant place over here is going to be the left child of 60.
Now you might be interested.
Why?
Because we have mentioned that binary heap is a complete heap.
Only the last level can be unfilled.
So in this case the nodes will be located as left as possible.
So as you can see here, for the first node we have two children.
We don't have any place.
And for the left subtree which is 80 we have two children.
And for the right subtree which is 70 we have two children.
So the next place is left child of the 60 over here and 100 will be inserted like this.
Now whenever we are inserting a new node to the binary heap, we are inserting it to the next vacant
place.
Now if we look at this in the array, it's going to be inserted at the end of the array.
Because from beginning till the end we have filled with these elements over here.
So in this case this means that we are going to use the arrays push method.
So this insert method will be declared inside binary heap class.
And it's going to take as a parameter value.
Then after passing the value is going to be this one.
For example let's say we are passing 100 over here.
Then it's going to be inserted at the next vacant place.
So we have said that the next vacant place is 60 Leftchild now 60, is located at the index of three.
And based on this index we can calculate the index of left child of 60, which is going to be two multiply
three plus one, which is going to be index of seven.
Now to be able to insert at the end of this array, all we have to do is we are just going to call the
array with push method with the value.
So we know that in JavaScript, push method will insert a new element at the end of the array over here
like this.
So this is how the insert method works.
So as you can see the insert method for binary heap is very simple method, but it is not as simple
as it seems because whenever we are inserting the hundred over here, you see that the main property
of the binary heap is violated.
So we have said that in case of max heaps, the biggest element will be located in the root and all
other elements will be less than the root.
And it's applicable for all subtrees over here.
But in this case we can easily see that 100 is the greatest element, but it is not located at the root.
So here, to maintain the binary heap property, we are going to use something called Heapify.
Heapify is an important operation used to maintain the heap property in binary tree after modification,
insertion or deletion.
So this means that here after insertion, we are going to check that if the main property is not maintained,
we are going to use the Heapify process.
This process restores the heap property by comparing the nodes and swapping them.
So here we are going to call the Heapify method.
After inserting it now, before continuing to create the Heapify method, first we need to create the
helper methods that we are going to use the inside Heapify method.
So here, to maintain the main property, the first thing that we are going to do, we are going to
compare 100 with its parent.
So we see that 100 is greater than its parent.
So this means that we are going to swap their places.
So this process will be heapify up.
So 100 is greater than 60.
We are just going to swap them.
So after swapping with 60 we have to swap them in the array over here.
So this is visualization and this is the implementation.
Then we are going to compare 100 with 80 because 80 is its parent.
So we see that 100 is greater than 80.
We are just going to swap them.
So after swapping it it's going to be swapped in the array.
Then one more time we are going to check 100 with its parent which is 90.
We see that 100 is greater than 90.
So we are going to swap it with 90 like this.
So after swapping it you will see that the main property of the heap is maintained.
So in case of max heaps the biggest element is located at the root of the heap over here.
Now the question is how can we swap these elements.
So for this we are going to have swap method As I mentioned, swap method is used to swap the nodes
like this.
So as shown you that in case of 100 it's going to be swapped until it reaches the root node.
Now the function itself is going to be something like this.
So as a parameter it's going to take the index of two elements.
So these are the elements that we want to swap.
And then we have this line over here.
This line performs the swap.
It sets the element at the index I to what was at index of j or vice versa.
So in this case the element which is located at the index of I will be placed at the index of j, and
the element which is located at the index of j will be placed at the index of I.
So based on these indexes we are going to swap the elements.
This method is very crucial in maintaining the heap property when inserting or removing the elements
from the heap, because it helps to reorder the heap to ensure that the parent child relationship meets
the heap.
Requirements.
Maximum or minimum heap.
Now, if you use this method in our heap that we have created before.
So we have inserted 100 over here.
So the first thing that we are going to do, we are going to call swap with the index of seven and three.
Now at the index of seven we had 100.
And at the index of three we had 60.
And they are swapped their places.
Now after doing so one more time we are going to call swap method with the index of three and one.
So at the index of three we have 100.
And at index of one we have the parent of 100 which is 80.
And this method will swap them.
Then one more time we are going to call swap method with the index of one and zero.
So at index of one we have 100 and at index of zero we have 90.
So their places will be swapped like this.
So that's how the swap method will work.
Now the question is how we know that we need to swap these two elements that is located in these indexes.
Now to be able to identify that we need to compare these two elements with each other.
Now for this we are going to have compare method.
Now compare method also takes as a parameter to indexes.
And these indexes will be the elements that we want to compare and depending on the type of the heap.
So we are going to check that if this is minimum heap or maximum heap, we are going to return like
this.
So in case of minimum heap, if the element at the index I is less than the element at the index of
j, meaning I should be above, meaning that the element which is located at the index of I should be
above the element which is located at the index of j in the heap.
So that's why in this case, in case of minimum heap, it's going to return true.
In case of maximum heap it's going to return true.
If the element at index I is greater than the element at index j, then it means that I should be above
j in the heap.
So in this case it's going to return true.
So based on the compare we are going to swap the elements so we can put it like this.
So I'm just going to bring the binary heap that we had before where we have inserted 100.
So in this case we are going to compare 100 with 60.
So as a parameter we are going to pass the index of 100 which is seven, and the index of its parent
which is 63.
And we compare them.
We see that in this case this is maxheap.
And the first index element, which is 100, is greater than the second index element which is 60.
In this case we are just going to call the swap method for them.
And this is going to swap these values like this.
Then one more time we are going to check that if the element which is located at the index of three,
which is 100, is greater than the element which is located at the index of 80.
We see that it is greater.
So we are going to call swap method for this one also with the same index.
And this is going to swap them.
And this will continue for the elements which is located at the index of one and zero.
So we see that it is greater.
So we are going to call swap method for these ones also.
So that's how the swap and compare method works in case of binary heap.
And these methods will be used in Heapify method that we are going to discuss in the next lecture.
So after inserting element we are going to call Heapify up method.
But when we are deleting the elements from the binary heap, we are going to call Heapify down method.
So let's head over to the next lecture to see how Heapify method works.
